State of the Trail
Teresa Patterson, Dale Harris, & Steve Smith,
Trinity Coalition

Trinity River National Water Trail
 One of 35 in the nation
 www.nps.gov/subjects/nationaltrailssystem/national-water-trails-
system.htm
 Select “Find Your National Water Trail”
 Select “Trinity River Paddling Trail”

Trinity River National
Water Trail
All but 2 sections are 4-6 miles in length
 One 12-mile section
 One 24-mile section
 New expansion sites will shorten some
of these distances

Paddling Trail Status May 2023
Currently 20 out of 21 launch sites are open
 Loop 12 closed - flood damage and safety
concerns
 One launch site on the West Fork is getting difficult
to use
 Portage trail around Carrollton Dam is being used
and paddling community is keeping it clean
Portage trail around Carrollton Dam

Future Launch Sites / Trail Additions
 New Beltline canoe launch
 New Viridian canoe launch
 New launch at Riverside Park in Fort Worth – in planning stages
 Trinity View Park canoe and kayak launch summer / Fall 2023

Paddling Trail Expansion
Dale Harris, Trinity Coalition

Paddling Trail Expansion
 Discussed possibility of adding USACE boat ramps on Corps lakes
Biggest issue is portaging around the Dams – some are over a mile
National Parks Service requires end to end continuity of the Water Trail
 Discussed with Trinity River Authority on a possible plan:
1. Lower Trinity / Lake Livingston to Trinity Bay
2. Loop 12 down to Malloy Bridge Rd. / Goat Island Preserve and Riverbend
Preserve
3. Malloy Bridge to Lake Livingston (long-term future)
 Drafted letter to be sent to Cornyn, Cruz, and Allred to use the “Bipartisan
Infrastructure Plan” to remove Lock & Dam #1
